headline: Every major above its 200-day, RSI screaming, and the crowd only at Greed, not Extreme
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and DOGE are all above their 200-day lines. Only ADA sits below, still down 75.9% from its 12-month high even after a 38.15% 30-day run. Six of seven majors agreeing on trend direction is not the norm, and it means the tape is not arguing with itself the way it often does.

But look at momentum against that trend and you find the first real tension. RSI-14 readings across the board are extreme: XRP at 85.9, SOL at 84.8, BTC at 82.7, BNB at 85.0, ETH at 80.4, DOGE at 79.8. Anything north of 70 is conventionally overbought, and these are well past that. MACD is above signal on every single asset, so the trend itself is still accelerating, not fading. That's the interesting part: usually RSI this stretched comes with some MACD hesitation, a rollover starting to show. Not here. The trend and the momentum are both pointing the same way, hard. That doesn't tell you when it cools, only that right now the move is not resting.

Positioning is calmer than the momentum board would suggest. BTC and ETH funding on OKX sit at just 0.01% per 8 hours (about 11% annualized), which is unremarkable, not the double-digit daily funding you see when leverage is truly overheated. Open interest is sizable ($2.35B on BTC, $1.48B on ETH) but the long/short account ratios tell a split story: BTC is nearly balanced at 1.02, while SOL (1.94), XRP (2.07) and especially DOGE (3.49) show crowds heavily tilted long. Liquidations in the last 24 hours skewed toward shorts getting run over on BTC ($10.8M shorts vs $6.3M longs) and ETH ($10.6M shorts vs $3.8M longs), consistent with a market that keeps punishing anyone betting against it. SOL and XRP flipped the other way, longs eating the liquidations there, a reminder that not every corner of this rally is friction-free.

Flows add another layer worth sitting with. BTC spot ETFs posted $307.5M net on Aug 21, and the five-session total is $1,917.8M, all same direction (5 of 5 days positive), a real traditional-finance bid. ETH ETFs echoed that with $184.0M on the day and $692.6M over five sessions. Whale activity over the last 48 hours shows $88.4M in BTC moving off exchanges (into a Kraken withdrawal, notably), while TRUMP token saw $24.9M moving onto Binance, the kind of divergence that says not every asset is being treated the same by large holders. Zoom out to the weekly whale series and the picture flips from the daily snapshot: the week ending Aug 3 saw $1,067M leave exchanges, but the two weeks after that reversed onto exchanges ($304M, then $187M), and the week ending Aug 24 shows $1,091M moving onto exchanges, the largest weekly onto-exchange print in the set. That's three straight weeks of net onto-exchange flow even as today's 48-hour BTC snapshot shows outflow. Worth naming plainly rather than smoothing over.

Sentiment sits at 73, labeled Greed, within a 30-day range that topped out exactly there (25 to 73). So the crowd is at the ceiling of its recent mood, but not in Extreme Greed territory, and it's arguably underreacting to a tape where RSI is pinned near 85 on multiple assets. Stablecoin float is flat over 30 days at $308.6B, meaning the dry powder pile itself isn't growing, even as prices run. That's a mild contradiction: rising prices, extended momentum, strong ETF pull, but the stablecoin base sitting still and the multi-week whale trend leaning toward exchanges rather than away from them.

What to watch from here: whether BTC funding stays anchored near 11% annualized or starts climbing as OI grows, whether the weekly whale flow prints another onto-exchange week or breaks the three-week streak, and whether MACD lines start to converge on any of these assets even as RSI stays stretched. A funding spike paired with a fourth straight onto-exchange week would be a different tape than the one sitting in front of you today.
